key_insight: KaliBench shows that translating natural-language intent into executable cybersecurity CLI commands is still very hard for LLMs, even when the task is narrowed to tool use rather than open-ended agent behavior.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark provides a reproducible way to train and evaluate models for real Kali Linux tool invocation, which is directly relevant to building reliable security copilots and autonomous penetration-testing agents.
method: 8,504 natural-language query–command pairs covering 1,642 Kali Linux tools
Manuscript-grounded dataset creation with deterministic canonicalization and alias-aware evaluation
Multi-stage verification using LLM checks, sandboxed terminal execution, and human refinement
evidence_signal: Across 24 model/configuration settings, no open-weight model exceeded 42% exact-command accuracy in the unrestricted setting, and the benchmark supports runtime-free verifiable rewards for training.
watch_item: Exact-command success is sensitive to syntax, flag binding, and argument order, so any deployment must preserve strict command validation and sandboxing to avoid unsafe or invalid execution.
paper_title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
